_comment: klt erc supply spec for the merged top cell -- T1 checklist item 11
('Power delivery, structural', klayout-tools#2025/#2057) requires a
supply-net read of this shape for every block (issue #300). See
layout/README.md's 'Item 11' section for the full account of what this
run showed and does not show; this block only justifies each field.
Run it against the committed top-cell GDS:
klt erc layout/cells/temp_por_top.gds \
layout/cells/temp_por_top.erc-supply-spec.json --format json
producing layout/reports/temp_por_top/erc_supply.json.
Why each field is shaped this way:
- `stackup[0]` MUST carry `role: "gate"` (klt erc's own contract), so the
stack starts at Poly2 rather than at Metal1. `active_layer` (Comp) makes
the gate-identification test `poly AND diff` instead of raw poly area,
which is what keeps this block's poly-resistor legs (temp_core's R2
ladder and bias_core's bias resistors -- real poly with no gate oxide)
out of `gates[]` (klayout-tools docs/cli/erc.md, 'Gate area: poly n diff
vs. raw poly area', issue #1979). This block has no filler/filltie
masters (it is hand-drawn analog, not a placed-and-routed standard-cell
flow), but the same poly-without-oxide shape appears here as resistors.
- Metal1 through Metal5 is this block's full drawn interconnect stack
(layout/build_cells.py's own header comment: 'Nwell 21/0 . Comp 22/0 .
so the supply read has to cover every level a rail or a riser could be
drawn on, not just the levels the top-level VDD/VSS rails happen to use.
- `label_layer` is declared on Metal1 (34/10) and Metal2 (36/10), and
deliberately NOT on Metal3/Metal4/Metal5 -- verified against this
block's own merged GDS with `klt layers --flattened --include-text`
rather than assumed from another block's spec:
* 34/10 carries 48 text occurrences, including 5 VDD + 5 VSS --
layout/build_cells.py's per-sub-cell internal net labels (each
sub-cell's own VDD/VSS pin, dropped on its own Metal1 riser; see
METAL1_LABEL, e.g. the bias_core/por_comparator/por_output_chain/
temp_core instances' own `b.label("VDD", ...)` / `b.label("VSS",
...)` calls).
* 36/10 carries 5 text occurrences: CTAT, PTAT, RESETn, VDD, VSS --
this is `_top_cell`'s own METAL2_LABEL set, i.e. the block's
RATIFIED 5-PAD PINOUT (layout/build_cells.py: 'the ratified 5-pad
pinout ... VDD/VSS are labelled on their rails ... the *only*
labels drawn directly in this cell'). This is the label set
`top_cell_pins` (klayout-tools#291) turns into the chip's own pin
list.
* Metal3 (42/0), Metal4 (46/0) and Metal5 (81/0) carry NO text at
all in this GDS (`text_count: 0` for every layer/datatype pair on
those levels) -- Metal5 in particular is drawn only as the MiM
capacitor plates' Via4 escape route in bias_core and
por_output_chain (layout/build_cells.py: 'Via3 40/0 . Via4 41/0 .
Metal5 81/0 (the drawn MiM units' plate routing, #264 -- ... the
top plate's only escape is Via4 -> Metal5 -> a second Via4 down a
fresh Metal4 island, both cells only)'), never a supply rail. This
is the opposite of the fleet's own digital-flow worked example
(gf180-drone-fc's layout/digital/erc-supply-spec.json labels
Metal1 and Metal5, because its PDN's top strap is on Metal5) --
the label_layer choice tracks what a block's own GDS actually
carries pin text on, not a fixed per-PDK convention.
- GDS layer numbers cross-checked two ways, per issue #300: against
layout/build_cells.py's own layer constants (already the numbers klt's
curated gf180mcu deck reads, per layout/README.md), AND independently
against the installed PDK's own tech file
(libs.tech/klayout/tech/gf180mcu.lyp): Poly2 30/0, COMP 22/0, Metal1
34/0, Metal1_Label 34/10, Metal2 36/0, Metal2_Label 36/10, Metal3 42/0,
Metal4 46/0, Metal5 81/0, Contact 33/0, Via1 35/0, Via2 38/0, Via3
40/0, Via4 41/0 -- every one of the 15 <source> entries matched
exactly.
- `vias[]` bridges every adjacent stackup pair with this PDK's own
contact/via layer, so a supply riser that only makes electrical sense
through a via (e.g. a Metal1 rail reached from a Metal2 label) is not
reported as disconnected purely because `klt erc`'s connectivity model
was never told the via exists.
- `nets[]`: VDD and VSS both `kind: "supply"`, which is what makes a
short between them report as the severe `erc.supply_short` rather than
the general `erc.multiply_driven_net`. Each must resolve to exactly
ONE electrical island: `erc.unconnected_net` fires on zero matches
(nothing in the layout carries that label at all) AND on more than one
(the rail is split into pieces that never touch) -- so ZERO findings of
that rule is exactly the 'one island per supply' verdict, not merely an
absence of a report.
- `devices[]` declares this block's drawn poly-resistor bodies so the
connectivity model stops reading them as wires (klayout-tools#2183,
fixed by klayout-tools#2205 at commit ddf47e78). `klt erc` traces
wire/via connectivity only -- it registers no device extraction -- so
without this declaration every drawn resistor body conducts across its
own extent, and a supply-sensing resistive divider across the rails (the
defining topology of a power-on-reset comparator, which this block is)
reports a FALSE `erc.supply_short` no matter how clean the layout is.
That is exactly what the first committed run of this spec showed; see
layout/README.md's 'Item 11' section for that history.
- `body_layer` is RES_MK (110/5), NOT the `Resistor` high-sheet-rho ID
layer (62/0), and the difference matters. 62/0 is only the *class*
selector that picks `ppolyf_u_1k` out of the resistor family: in this
GDS it is drawn on 251 shapes, all of them in `bias_core` (24) and
`por_comparator` (227), and NONE in `temp_core` -- whose R2 gain-ladder
segments are plain `ppolyf_u` bodies (layout/build_cells.py's
`_r_segment` draws PPLUS/SAB/RES_MK and no 62/0). RES_MK is the deck's
resistor-*candidate* marker, required for every recognised flavour, and
is drawn on all 301 body shapes (bias_core 24 + por_comparator 227 +
temp_core 50). Measured on this GDS: RES_MK n Poly2 = 50526.34 um2
versus Resistor(62/0) n Poly2 = 41858.34 um2 -- declaring 62/0 alone
would leave 8668.00 um2 of real resistor body still modelled as wire.
Both clear the false `erc.supply_short`; only RES_MK describes the
layout completely, so RES_MK is what is declared.
- Over-coverage cross-check, per `klt erc`'s own warning that the
subtraction is purely geometric ('it cuts, so declare it where the
device is'): RES_MK n (Poly2 n Comp) = 0.000 um2, i.e. the carve-out
removes no gate region at all, and the run reports zero
`erc.unconnected_net` and zero `erc.floating_gate`. Note that
`provenance.devices[0].body_area_um2` reads 53126.74, which is RES_MK's
own merged area rather than the 50526.34 um2 actually subtracted from
Poly2 -- the 2600.40 um2 difference is `_r_segment`'s deliberate
+/-0.3 um marker overhang in x, which sits over no conductor and so
subtracts nothing. That the field reports the marker area rather than
the subtracted area is an upstream reporting gap, filed generically as
klayout-tools#2226; it does not affect this run's verdict, but it is
why the area cross-check above was measured independently rather than
read out of the report.
- `ties[]` (T1 item 11, issue #310) declares every substrate/well tie
this block draws, now that the tie-collapse bug that justified omitting
it (klayout-tools#2169: a blanket drawn well self-connected and merged
the whole routed design into one island) is fixed upstream. Four
entries, one per electrically distinct tie population -- verified by
loading this block's own merged GDS with `klayout.db` and checking each
tap_boxes narrowing in isolation before combining them (no entry here
was written by inspection of the drawn geometry alone):
1. `device_body_wells` -> VDD: every ordinary PMOS device-body Nwell
in the design -- `temp_core`'s NW1 (the cascoded-mirror/startup
network), `bias_core`'s PMOS row, `por_comparator`'s PMOS row and
its instanced `por_comparator_bias_okb_inv`, `por_output_chain`'s
PMOS row. `well_excludes: ["127/5"]` drops the two vertical-PNP
base tubs (DRC_BJT-marked) from this class; `well_excludes_boxes`
additionally drops `temp_core`'s NW2 (the differential input
pair's shared well -- see `nw2_tail_well` below), since neither a
drawn marker nor a DRC_BJT patch distinguishes NW2 from NW1 on the
same layer. Nplus (32/0) and Pplus (31/0) are drawn on NO device-row
comp in this stream (`_mos_finger` draws no implant at all -- only
the R2/bias resistor bodies and the PNP array's own emitter/base/
collector rings carry an implant marker), so `tap_requires` cannot
name a real tap boolean here (klayout-tools#2199/#2234): every
`tap_boxes` entry is instead a caller assertion of exactly where
each well's own dedicated VDD tie-strap comp sits --
`layout/build_cells.py`'s `tie_y0`/`tie_y1` strap for `bias_core`/
`por_comparator`/`por_output_chain` (a comp rectangle physically
separate from the PMOS row's own source/drain comp, clear of every
device terminal), the instanced inverter's own small PMOS source
half, and -- `temp_core`'s NW1 draws no separate strap at all -- the
source-side half of `XMT`'s own comp (`design/netlist/temp_core.
spice`: source net `VDD`, the first device in NW1's row). Each box
is narrow enough to exclude the neighbouring drain/other-net comp on
the same drawn shape (never the whole device), which is what keeps
the tap non-degenerate under klayout-tools#2199's geometric test
(an assertion that removes nothing from the drawn comp inside the
well grades as skipped, not checked) -- and, independently, what
keeps the comp registered into the connectivity graph from spanning
a whole row's worth of unrelated nets and manufacturing a false
tie for an adjacent, genuinely untied well (verified directly: an
unnarrowed `tap_is_dedicated: true` probe against this same stream
merges `BIAS_OK`/`IBIAS`/`VDD`/`VREF` into one net and reports every
well tied to everything, because `klt erc`'s connectivity model has
no gate-blocks-diffusion rule -- a drawn gate never divides a comp
region registered as one tap, so an unclipped well-wide tap shorts
every source/drain island it touches; narrow, per-tap boxes are the
only safe declaration on this implant-free stream, not a stylistic
choice).
2. `pnp_base_tubs` -> VSS: the two vertical-PNP arrays' own base tubs
(`temp_core`'s rank-3 centroid array and `bias_core`'s own array),
selected by `well_requires: ["127/5"]` (DRC_BJT) -- a falsifiable
selection, since it keeps exactly these 2 of the design's 8 drawn
Nwell shapes, never all 8 or none. Both arrays' base rings are
diode-connected to their own collector substrate ring, which is
why the base -- unlike every device-body well above -- ties to VSS,
not VDD (`layout/build_cells.py`'s `_temp_core_pnp_array` docstring:
'both rings down to VSS'). `tap_boxes` names each array's own base-
tap ring segments (`temp_core`'s inner Nplus-marked ring, `bias_core`'s
plain-comp ring -- the two arrays use different tap constructions,
so a shared `tap_requires` cannot cover both without either missing
`bias_core`'s tap or, worse, degenerating silently), never the
rings' own enclosing rectangle, which would also sweep in the 9/10
emitter comp squares each ring encloses -- real device terminals
wired to `NC`/`NA`/`EC`/`ER`, not taps, and shorting them into the
tap net would be exactly the false-tie mechanism `devices[]` already
exists to prevent one level up (this time via an over-broad tap
assertion rather than an un-declared device body).
3. `nw2_tail_well` -> NT: `temp_core`'s differential-pair well, which
this design deliberately body-ties to the pair's own shared tail
node (`NT`, not VDD -- a standard body-effect-cancellation move for
a matched input pair) rather than the supply. Confirmed from
`_TEMP_CORE_ROW`: every one of NW2's six fingers (two edge dummies
plus `XMI1`/`XMI2`'s common-centroid legs) names `NT` as its source,
none names VDD -- and `NT` carries its own Metal1 label inside
`temp_core` (`klt layers --flattened --include-text` on 34/10),
so the tie is independently checkable, not merely asserted.
`well_excludes: ["127/5"]` plus `well_requires_boxes` (naming NW2's
own drawn extent) isolate exactly this one shape; `tap_boxes` names
the source-side half of each of the six fingers' own comp (the
drain half of the same shape, on `N1`/`N2`/`NT`'s *other* appearance
as a drain, is excluded, same non-degeneracy reasoning as class 1).
4. `substrate_tie` -> VSS, `well_layer: null` + `well_boxes`
(klayout-tools#2255): the deck draws no p-well/p-substrate layer at
all, so every native-substrate tie in this design -- the outer
perimeter guard ring, the domain-seam moat, each of `bias_core`'s/
`por_comparator`'s/`por_output_chain`'s own guard rings, and
`temp_core`'s PNP arrays' outer (Pplus) collector rings -- has
nothing to name as a drawn well. `well_boxes` asserts each ring's
own four edge segments (never the ring's enclosing rectangle, which
for the outer perimeter ring is within 1% of the whole top cell's
own extent and would grade `degenerate_well_assertion` per
klayout-tools#2255's own falsifiability test -- and, for every
ring, would also sweep in the guard-ringed interior's real devices);
`well_boxes`' 21 segments, across 6 separate rings/strips, merge
into 6 independent polygons (none of the rings touch each other),
so `erc.missing_tie` grades each ring on its own evidence, not on
whichever ring happens to pass. `tap_boxes` narrows each segment to
its own centre third, clear of the segment's own outer/inner edge,
which is enough to keep the narrowing non-degenerate without
excluding the ring's own contact row (every guard ring/moat segment
here is contacted along its centreline at 1 um pitch --
`layout/build_cells.py`'s `_draw_guard_ring`/`_top_guard_ring`/
`_guard_ring_segments`). `layout/floorplan.md`'s own guard-ring/moat
account (`layout/README.md`'s former Item 11 stand-in evidence,
superseded by this declaration) is the design source these
coordinates were taken from, cross-checked against the committed
GDS directly rather than against that account's prose.
Falsifiability, checked directly against this GDS rather than assumed.
Three different ways to break a tie produce three different signals,
and the experiment a reader is most likely to reach for first -- case 3
-- produces NO finding at all, so all three are spelled out:
1. Deleting the tap box(es) that tie exactly ONE well/tub/ring, leaving
the rest of that entry's `tap_boxes` intact (a cut strap on a single
region), reports a real `erc.missing_tie` -- description 'well/tub
region has no <tie name> tap contact drawn inside it' -- scoped to
exactly that region's own bbox, with every other declared tie
unaffected, including when the broken tie shares its `well_layer`,
its `net`, or both with a genuinely-tied entry elsewhere in this
same array. Confirmed one region at a time for all five of
`device_body_wells`' wells, for each of `pnp_base_tubs`' two base
tubs, and for a whole `substrate_tie` ring: exactly one finding
each, on that region's bbox, `erc_coverage.skipped` still empty.
2. Declaring a tie's `net` WRONG also reports `erc.missing_tie`, with a
different description ('well/tub tap is not connected to declared
net ...') and likewise scoped per region: declaring `nw2_tail_well`
as `VDD` instead of `NT` yields exactly one finding, on NW2's own
bbox. That is the independent check that `NT` -- not the supply --
really is this well's body tie.
3. Emptying a whole `tap_boxes` array (`[]`, or dropping the key) is
NOT an `erc.missing_tie` and must not be described as one. A tap
assertion that narrows nothing grades `degenerate_tap_declaration`
(klayout-tools#2199), so the entry moves into `erc_coverage.skipped`
and `erc_status` degrades to `clean_partial` while `erc_findings`
and `erc_finding_count` stay at zero -- confirmed for all four
entries. That is still a real guard (the degradation is loud, never
a silent clean), but it is a COVERAGE signal rather than a verdict
finding, which is why item 11's pass condition has to be read as
zero findings AND `erc_coverage.skipped: []` AND `erc_status:
clean`, never the finding count alone.
Deleting a SINGLE segment of a multi-segment tie leaves the report
fully clean (`erc_status: clean`, `skipped: []`), by construction and
not as a gap: each `substrate_tie` ring is asserted by four edge
segments and the remaining three still tie it, and NW2 carries six
finger taps for the one well. The sensitivity this declaration has is
per-region (case 1), not per-segment; a per-segment claim would
overstate it.
No tie here was narrowed to make a real finding disappear; narrower
alternatives for every class above were tried first and rejected
specifically because they produced a false pass, a false fail, or a
skipped/degenerate grading rather than a checked one (see the per-class
notes above).
Toolchain note: `well_requires`/`well_excludes` (issue #2339) and
`well_requires_boxes`/`well_excludes_boxes` (issue #2540) -- both load-
bearing for classes 1-3 above -- postdate the `klt 0.6.0` *tag*
(`v0.6.0`, commit c622e8ad, 2026-09-22): neither key exists in that
release's `erc.py`, confirmed by reading it directly at the tag. This
run therefore answers to the same kind of newer-than-any-release build
`layout/README.md`'s 'Toolchain note' section already documents for
this report's first (`ties`-less) version -- see that section, updated
for this run, for the exact commit and why `layout/toolchain.json`'s
pin and `layout/run_checks.sh`'s `toolchain_gate` are unaffected (both
answer for `klt drc`'s curated deck, never for `klt erc`, which reads
only this spec's own declared layers).
